jobs.title: Postdoc Positions in Particle Physics
jobs.description:
The Center for Particle Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology (NNU-PP) at
   Nanjing Normal University invites applications for 1-2 postdoctoral
   research positions. We seek outstanding candidates to join our group
   in one or more of the following areas, including but not limited to:

     * Higgs Physics

     * Cosmological Phase Transition

     * Gravitational Wave

     * Baryogenesis

     * AI4Science

   About NNU-PP
   Our research center hosts an active and dynamic group of researchers,
   including faculty members Ariel Arza, Peter Athron, Ning Liu,
   Chih-Ting Lu, Lei Wu, and Yongcheng Wu. We offer a collaborative
   environment with ample opportunities for academic growth and
   interdisciplinary research.
   Position Details

     * Appointment: Initial term of 2 years, with a possibility of
       renewal for a third year based on performance.

     * Salary and Benefits:

       * Competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
         experience.

       * Subsidized housing options through the university.

       * Exceptional candidates will be nominated for the prestigious
         China/Jiangsu Province Postdoctoral Innovative Talent Support
         Program. Successful nominees will receive enhanced benefits,
         including a significantly increased stipend and a dedicated
         travel budget, with the total annual salary package reaching up
         to 600,000 RMB/year.

   Application Requirements
   Interested candidates should prepare the following documents:

     1. Curriculum Vitae (CV)

     2. Publication List

     3. Research Statement (outlining past work and future plans)

   Applicants should also arrange for three reference letters to be
   submitted directly through Academic Jobs Online (AJO).
   Application Deadline
   All applications should be submitted no later than 2026/01/31. We look
   forward to receiving your application and welcoming you to our dynamic
   team at NNU-PP. For further information about the center and the
   position, please contact us via ycwu@njnu.edu.cn

jobs.title: Postdoc position in theoretical particle physics
jobs.description:
A 2+1 year postdoctoral position is open in the field of theoretical particle physics. The research project aims
at providing high-precision theoretical predictions for Today's and Tomorrow's particle accelerators.
To do so the framework of quantum field theory would be used, in particular perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics.

The position will take place at the Eotvos University (ELTE) in Budapest, Hungary.

Our research group seeks its new postdoc with strong foundation in theoretical particle physics. The
postdoc should also be fluent in English. PhD in perturbative QCD or electroweak corrections takes precedence.

The selected postdoc would receive the following benefits:
- Participating in state-of-art calculations important for the field
- Being part of a young, motivated and energetic research group and also part of a large, impactful international
  collaboration
- The position is research only (no teaching nor administrative duties)
- Competitive salary

The starting date is flexible it can be as early as March, 2026.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
The Particle Physics, Nuclear Physics, and Astrophysics Group in the Department of Physics at Tsinghua University invites applications for tenure-track faculty positions in particle physics, nuclear physics, and cosmology.

Faculty members in the Department of Physics at Tsinghua University are expected to conduct independent, forefront research and supervise both Ph.D. and undergraduate students. The positions are open to researchers of all nationalities and offer an internationally competitive salary, housing subsidy, and start-up funds. The expected start date is September 2026, with flexibility.

Applications should be submitted via AcademicJobsOnline (AJO). For full consideration, all application materials should be received by December 31, 2025. The search will remain open until the positions are filled.

jobs.title: Postdoc in theoretical high-energy physics and astroparticle physics
jobs.description:
The High Energy Theory group at the University of Utah invites
   applications for one or more postdoctoral positions to begin in
   approximately August 2026. Areas of specialization include theoretical
   and phenomenological high energy physics and astroparticle physics.
   Successful applicants will have research interests that overlap with
   those of Professors Gustavo Marques-Tavares, Pearl Sandick, and/or
   Zhengkang Zhang. Additional faculty in the High Energy Theory group
   include Professor Paolo Gondolo and Emeritus Professors Carleton DeTar
   and Yong-Shi Wu. You can learn more about research in the High Energy
   Theory group as well as other related research in the Department of
   Physics and Astronomy at https://www.physics.utah.edu/research/.
   Postdoctoral appointment(s) are annual and renewable for up to three
   years contingent on satisfactory performance and the availability of
   continued funding. Your complete application must include a CV,
   publication list, statement of research interests, and 3-5 reference
   letters. Complete applications received by December 15, 2025 will
   receive first consideration. Applications submitted after December 15
   will be considered only as long as a position is available.
   ******************************

jobs.title: Tufts University, Tufts Institute of Cosmology, Postdoctoral Scholar
jobs.description:
The Tufts Institute of Cosmology at Tufts University invites applications
   for one postdoctoral researcher position starting in September 2026.
   The position is a full-time, 24-month (two-year) appointment, which
   may be extended to a third year upon successful performance,
   availability of funding, and mutual agreement. The research is
   expected to be at the interface of theoretical cosmology and particle
   physics, including but not limited to early universe cosmology,
   aspects of dark matter, including axions and other models,
   gravitational waves, and applications of effective field theory. The
   faculty members in the cosmology group are Mark Hertzberg, Soubhik
   Kumar, and Ken Olum. The group also includes other postdocs, long-term
   visitors, and graduate students, and has a joint seminar series with
   MIT. The group also maintains strong connections with other cosmology
   and particle theory research groups in the greater Boston area, and
   such collaborations will be highly encouraged. More information about
   the group is available at
   https://as.tufts.edu/physics/tufts-institute-cosmology. Applicants are
   invited to send a cover letter, CV, a publication list, a statement of
   research interests (three pages maximum plus references), and arrange
   for three letters of reference to be sent via AJO. Applications
   received by December 15, 2025, will be given full consideration. For
   questions about this position, please contact Soubhik Kumar
   (soubhik.kumar (at) tufts.edu). Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
   Tufts University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. See the
   University’s Non-Discrimination statement and policy here
   https://oeo.tufts.edu/policies-procedures/non-discrimination/. If you
   are an applicant with a disability who is unable to use our online
   tools to search and apply for jobs, please contact us by calling the
   Office of Equal Opportunity (OEO) at 617-627-3298 or at oeo@tufts.edu.
   Applicants can learn more about requesting reasonable accommodations
   at https://oeo.tufts.edu/. Members of underrepresented groups are
   strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Joint Postdoctoral Position in AI for Theoretical Physics at Perimeter Institute and UW Madison
jobs.description:
The University of Wisconsin-Madison Physics Department (https://www.physics.wisc.edu/)
   and the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics (https://perimeterinstitute.ca/)
   invite applications for a joint 3-year postdoctoral position in AI for
   theoretical physics. The selected postdoc will spend the first year at
   UW Madison and the following two years at Perimeter Institute, with
   frequent travels in both directions. We are looking for candidates
   with a background in any area of theoretical physics and a strong
   interest in AI Reasoning. Prior publications in AI for physics are a
   bonus but not required. We are broadly interested in doing theoretical
   physics with AI Reasoning models. Topics of interest include: -
   Agentic approaches and test-time scaling methods. - Symbolic
   verification and tool usage. - Methods for novel research in
   theoretical physics with LLMs (e.g. combining LLMs with tree search or
   evolutionary algorithms). - Developing training and benchmarking data
   (e.g. https://tpbench.org/). - Fine-tuning of models with
   Reinforcement learning. In Madison, the postdoc will work in
   particular with the groups of Moritz Münchmeyer (https://munchmeyer.physics.wisc.edu/)
   and Gary Shiu (https://shiu.physics.wisc.edu/), and join an ongoing
   collaboration between physicists and computer scientists. At Perimeter
   Institute, the postdoc will be free to work with any faculty member.
   For questions about the position, please contact Moritz Münchmeyer at
   UW Madison (muenchmeyer@wisc.edu) or Kendrick Smith at Perimeter
   Institute (kmsmith@perimeterinstitute.ca). To apply, please submit a
   Research Statement, CV, Publication List and three reference letters
   by 2025/12/08 here on this website.

jobs.title: Postdoc
jobs.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
jobs.description:
The Taiwan Electron-Ion Collider Physics Project is soliciting
   applications for one experimental postdoc position. The successful
   candidate will work on developing the ZDC detector in the U.S. EIC
   far-forward detector system, applying the machine learning technique
   to the detector simulation as well as the relevant global analyses of
   the pion/kaon PDFs and proton TMDs. The duration of this position is
   initially two years, with the possibility of extending into the third
   year depending on performance. The position will be co-hosted by
   Academia Sinica and National Central University, and the successful
   candidate will be expected to start as soon as possible. To apply,
   please visit the academicjobsonline page at
   https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/31117 or send an email
   directly to Prof. C.-J. David Lin, dlin@nycu.edu.tw For inquiry,
   please contact any of the senior members on the project: * Prof.
   Wen-Chen Chang, changwc@phys.sinica.edu.tw * Prof. Chia-Ming Kuo,
   cmkuo@phy.ncu.edu.tw * Prof. Po-Ju Lin, pjlin@cc.ncu.edu.tw

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
jobs.description:
The Particle Theory and Cosmology Group at the Department of Physics,
   Tohoku University, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in
   the areas of quantum field theory, string theory and mathematical
   physics. In particular, candidates who are interested in topological
   aspects of quantum field theory and string theory are strongly
   encouraged to apply.
   The position will be funded by JST FOREST Program (Grant Number
   JPMJFR2030, Japan). Term of employment is up to 18 months from the
   date of appointment; however, employment will not be extended beyond
   March 31, 2028
   The applications should include(1) curriculum vitae, (2) research
   statement, (3) publication list, (4) two or more letters of
   recommendation. They should be uploaded via Academic Jobs Online.
   Application documents can be either in English or Japanese. Please
   submit the applications and letters by December 21, 2025.

jobs.title: McDonald Institute - CITA Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Winnipeg
jobs.description:
The Winnipeg Particle Theory Group is inviting applications for a
   three-year MI-CITA Theory Postdoctoral Fellowship in the field of
   particle cosmology, to work with Evan McDonough. Top-ranked
   applications will be sent to the MI-CITA Theory Evaluation committee,
   who will allocate fellowships. First round offers will be made in
   December. The Winnipeg Particle Theory Group is committed to
   diversity, equity, and inclusion, and especially welcomes applications
   from racialized persons/persons of colour, women,
   Indigenous/Aboriginal People of North America, persons with
   disabilities, LGBTQ2S+ persons, and others who may contribute to the
   further diversification of ideas. Prof. McDonough is an Associate
   Professor at the University of Winnipeg. McDonough is an active
   researcher and an active member of the research community: he is
   currently serving a 4-year term on the Council of the Canadian
   Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics (CITA), recently completed a
   two-year term as the Director of the Winnipeg Institute for
   Theoretical Physics, and recently completed a 3-year term on the
   Scientific Council of the Canadian national Institute for Particle
   Physics. McDonough is very invested in the success of students and
   postdocs, and works actively and deliberately to support both their
   professional success and personal happiness. You can find more about
   Evan, including recordings of research presentations, here:
   https://www.evanmcdonoughphysics.com/. An up-to-date list of papers by
   Evan can be found here: https://inspirehep.net/authors/1272159 . The
   MI-CITA Postdoc will play an integral role in all activities of the
   group, including leading high-profile projects, mentorship and
   research supervision of students across all levels (undergraduate,
   MSc, PhD), and will have many opportunities for professional
   development. Applicants are requested to identify their expertise in
   at least two of the following areas: -- Data analysis, in particular
   MCMC analyses of cosmological models (dark matter, dark energy) and
   data sets (CMB, LSS, etc). -- Cosmic Inflation model building and
   phenomenology, in particular inflation with connections to dark matter
   production mechanisms, such as gravitational particle production and
   primordial black hole dark matter production. -- Dark Matter model
   building, particularly novel dark matter production mechanisms --
   Ultralight dark matter model building and phenomenology, including
   axions and fuzzy dark matter -- String theory and supergravity
   cosmological model building Interested candidates should submit their
   application via academic jobs online. A complete application will
   consist of: -- a brief cover letter which identifies two or more of
   the above mentioned topics as areas of expertise. -- research
   statement. -- CV -- three letters of recommendation to be submitted on
   Academic Jobs Online. The deadline for applications is November 21,
   2025. The McDonald Institute expects applicants to complete a short,
   voluntary demographic survey to support the McDonald Institute's
   Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Indigenization (EDII) efforts.
   Information collected will support future efforts to promote MI
   opportunities to diverse communities. Your individual responses will
   be kept confidential and will have no impact on your candidacy.
   https://queensu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FPUBsNJGXrnyPc

jobs.title: Postdoctoral position in Theoretical Particle Physics at the IPhT (CNRS/CEA Saclay) and LPTHE (Sorbonne Université/CNRS)
jobs.description:
The Institut de Physique Théorique (IPhT) of the CEA/Saclay and the
   Laboratoire de Physique Théorique des Hautes Energies (LPTHE) of the
   Sorbonne Université invite applications for a postdoctoral research
   position in Theoretical Particle Physics, funded by the ANR P2S2
   project.
   The position is available initially for a fixed-term duration of 2
   years, with the possibility of extension for 1 further year.
   The P2S2 project aims at developing parton-shower algorithms with
   unprecedented (logarithmic) accuracy for jet substructure at the LHC.
   The project also has connections with analytic resummations and
   studies of jet substructure observables.
   The selected candidate will work with Gregory Soyez at the IPhT and
   Matteo Cacciari at the LPTHE, both in the Paris area. Both institutes
   have a strong QCD and particle physics group and the postdoc will be
   able to spend time at both locations.
   Applicants should hold a PhD in Physics, or be close to completion,
   and ideally have a strong background in perturbative quantum
   chromodynamics (QCD) at particle colliders. Candidates are expected to
   demonstrate a capacity for independent research work and should have a
   publication record commensurate with their career stage.
   Applications are to be submitted through Academic Jobs Online. The
   application consists of

     *  a cover letter,

     * a CV and a list of publications,

     * a description of the research achievements,

     * 3 reference letters.

   All the documents submitted should be in PDF format. Only applications
   received by Friday the 12th of December 2025 will be considered.
   Please direct inquiries about the position to Gregory Soyez (gregory.soyez@ipht.fr)
   and/or Matteo Cacciari (cacciari@lpthe.jussieu.fr).

jobs.title: 2025-3 Recruitment Announcement for Senior Researcher Positions at the CTPU-CGA (Cosmology, Gravity, and Astroparticle physics)
jobs.description:
The Center for Theoretical Physics of the Universe, Cosmology, Gravity,
   and Astroparticle Physics Group (CTPU-CGA) at Institute for Basic
   Science (http://www.ibs.re.kr/ctpu-cga), South Korea, invites
   applications for senior researcher positions in Theoretical Cosmology,
   Gravity and Astro(particle) physics, which can start before December
   16th, 2026 as long as all requirements are met at the point of
   starting time.* The position can preferably begin from October 1st,
   2026 though earlier appointment is negotiable. Any field and/or topic
   is welcome as long as it is related to cosmology, gravity, and
   (astro)particle physics. For example, observational cosmology, dark
   matter, neutrino physics, quantum information, and so on are also
   welcome in addition to standard theoretical cosmology, gravity, and
   particle physics. We recently initiated a new center called CTPU-CGA
   in CTPU led by the director, Masahide Yamaguchi, from March 2023. We
   will jointly organize the CTPU with another center CTPU-PTC led by the
   director, Kiwoon Choi, but the budget, organization, and recruitment
   are completely independent. The official language at the center is
   English. Research interests of our group cover broad areas of
   theoretical cosmology, gravity, astroparticle physics, and related
   areas. Applications should include CV(see the detailed requirement),
   publication list, research statement, Consent to Collection and Use of
   Personal Information / Application for IBS (download on IBS job
   Board), and at least three letters of recommendation. For full
   consideration, application materials including the letters should be

   Fellow (YSF) program. Accordingly, we are also recruiting a researcher
   affiliated with YSF. If your research topic is close to that of Dr.

   date) -Major: Physics CTPU-CGA (Daejeon, HQ) -No. of openings: 1 You

   Description - (Senior Researcher) Research-oriented personnel with a

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in HEP/QIS Theory
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Research AssociateHigh Energy/Quantum Information Science
   Theory Department of Physics University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
   The Department of Physics at the University of Illinois
   Urbana-Champaign invites applications for a postdoctoral research
   position in the HEP/QIS theory group. Areas of interest include, but
   are not limited to:

     * Formulating digital and analog simulations of lattice gauge
       theories on quantum hardware

     * Developing general-purpose algorithms and optimizations for
       Hamiltonian simulation

     * Developing new applications of quantum computing to HEP

   The successful applicant will collaborate with HEP/QIS group leaders
   Patrick Draper and Aida El-Khadra and students in the group on
   research related to the areas above. The hired candidate will also be
   a member of IQUIST, a large quantum research center at Illinois
   facilitating collaboration across all areas of quantum research.

   Candidates should have a Ph.D. awarded within the last 10 years, and
   must apply via Academic Jobs Online (AJO) by December 15, 2025 to
   receive full consideration. Candidates should submit a curriculum
   vitae including a list of publications, a research statement, and
   arrange to have at least three reference letters sent through AJO. If
   you have any questions or concerns, please contact Tonya Ayers (ayers1@illinois.edu).
   The University of Illinois offers a competitive benefits portfolio,
   depending on the position. Click for a complete list of Employee
   Benefits. The U of I is an EEO Employer/Vet/Disabled that participates
   in the federal e-Verify program and participates in a background check
   program focused on prior criminal or sexual misconduct history.
   Applicants with disabilities are encouraged to apply and may request a
   reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act
   (2008) to complete the application and/or interview process. Requests
   may be submitted through the reasonable accommodations portal, or by
   contacting the Accessibility & Accommodations Division of the Office
   for Access and Equity at 217-333-0885, or by emailing
   accessibility@illinois.edu.
   *Note that there is a second HEP/QIS position at Illinois, focused on
   dark matter and other new physics searches enabled by quantum sensing:
   ${JobURL}.
